recipes.name: Jamie's Cranberry Spinach Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 pound spinach, rinsed and torn into bite-size pieces

steps.text: Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook and stir almonds in butter until lightly toasted. Remove from heat and let cool.
Make dressing: Whisk together oil, sugar, cider vinegar, white wine vinegar, sesame seeds, poppy seeds, minced onion, and paprika in a medium bowl.
Combine spinach with toasted almonds and cranberries in a large serving bowl. Pour dressing over spinach mixture; toss well.

raw_recipe.headline: Jamie's Cranberry Spinach Salad
raw_recipe.description: This spinach salad is packed with fresh spinach, toasted almonds, and dried cranberries tossed with a sweet and tangy homemade poppy seed dressing.

review.reviewBody: When I saw this recipe's ingredients, I wondered what the fuss was about. Today, as I eat yesterday's wilted leftovers from a Tupperware container at 9am in the morning, I thought I'd write a review! I make this salad all the time now. I use spinach and other greens. I use toasted (10 minutes in 350 oven - no butter) pine nuts now insead of the almonds and will never go back - they are perfect for this salad. I add one container of blue cheese (a must for us - perfect blend of flavors). I use one 6 oz package Craisins. I've never used the poppy seeds - but the toasted sesame seeds (also at 350 for 10 minutes) are a must. I may or may not use dried minced onion. Toss all dressing ingredients in a container with a lid - and shake! This salad has been a hit with everyone I've served it to - dinner party, Easter lunch, dinner at home. It is so easy and easy to transport, too - just add the dressing once you get to where you're going. Try it - I bet you'll love it!!

WOW! AWESOME! TIME saver tips: use Paul Newman's balsamic vinagrette instead of making your own dressing. MONEY saving tip: use "Craisins" dried cranberry fruit instead of regular dried cranberries. Use can of mandarin oranges instead of poppy seeds. THIS WAS A HIT!

One of my favourite salad recipes, and I have lots. However, I alter it a bit by adding a cubed cooked beet and 1 cubed apple. I fry 1 cup of crushed walnuts until lightly brown then continue to fry briefly with 4 TBSP of maple syrup (easier than caramelizing almonds and kids love them), then let cool and break them up. The best part is adding chunks of goat cheese. This combination is great with this salad dressing and other ingredients. You can decrease the amount of sugar in this dressing a tad. It’s quite sweet, and there’s enough sweetness with the apples, walnuts and cranberries. If not, it still tastes fantastic.

Tossed this salad minus 1/4 cup of the dressing, put it in a spinach wrap (made 10) with sliced chicken breast (slowly roasted in olive oil, garlic, salt, white pepper & onions) and sold it on my food cart. Everyone that tried it said it’s a “must stay” on the menu. Thank you!

I would have rated this a 5 star if the dressing was not so tangy (too much vinegar). I made the initial version and found it too vinegary. I cut back on the vinegar and increased the oil, so my ratio was 3 parts oil to 1 part vinegar. Since the total liquid amount was 1 cup, I used 3/4 c olive oil and 1/8 cup of each of the vinegars listed. I also cut back on the sugar. I loved all the other ingredients used, especially the seeds. Thanks!

TLDR: The dressing is too sweet so add less sugar and definitely add blue cheese crumbles. I was really unsure about the dressing. After a few hours in the fridge, I went to pour it onto the salad and the vinegar smell seemed overpowering, but it doesn’t taste overly vinegary. I love anything sweet, but the dressing was too sweet even for my taste, which I would’ve thought was impossible. Next time, I’ll cut down on the sugar. I added blue cheese crumbles and I can’t imagine the salad without them. They add a tang & saltiness that offsets the sweetness of the cranberries and dressing. I’ll definitely make it again.

I used a low carb version, unsweetened cranberries, no raisins, and skipped sugar altogether. Carbs are a part of the nutritional panel and that includes sugar if using. Added feta cheese for more flavor. I have diabetes and have to watch my carbs intake closely. This salad turned out very good without all the added carbs.

I loved the blend of ingredients, but the dressing was too sweet. Next time I make this, I will cut the sugar by 1/2. The only changes I made was that I added sliced mushrooms to the salad and browned the almonds in the microwave, stirring every 30 seconds until browned.

I love simple salads like this! I made a single serve salad, subbed a stevia blend for the sugar, and used sliced almonds instead of slivered. So delicious! But after tasting it, I added a little feta cheese which took it over the top!

Everyone loved this and asked for the recipe. The two things that I would do differently next time: 1) There is too much dressing made. I would probably 1/2 the amount of dressing so it was a little lighter. 2) I would probably add it to each salad separately because the next day it wilts the spinach. However, it also could have been a result of #1.

Loved it!!! I will make this again!!!

Six stars! Toasted the almonds (skipped the butter). Did not have sesame or poppy seeds and it was still awesome. Added some chopped pecans to compensate. Also added a can of mandarin oranges like others suggested. Only used 1/4 cup sugar. Next time I will add less than 1/2 cup oil. I think it would be great with cheese, too. (maybe feta?)
I cheated and chopped red onions and used poppy seed store bought dressing. Would have been good to have added shelled sunflower seeds.
This salad is fantastic! My family loved it and I’ve now made it several times.

I made this to take to a Christmas pot luck pizza party. There was none left and everyone loved it. I used slivered and roasted almonds cut in half and stevia 2 tablespoons vs using sugar. I would make this again.
Loved the salad--I added fresh orange segments to the salad & some zest & a squeeze of juice tothe drrssing. I love the cranberry/,orange combo during the holidays

I have made this salad every holiday for about 15 years... upon request of family! Through the years I have changed a few things like skipping the cranberry and adding fresh fruit like blackberries and raspberries. It is not a holiday without this salad.
Add blue cheese or feta? Whole different level

I love the dressing but when I make it I use 1/4 cup sugar and it is still really sweet! I didn’t have almonds so I used a diced up sweet apple. Very delicious! I also sprinkle on chopped walnuts and feta cheese!😋

I was really surprised as to how amazing this tasted! I am allergic to almonds, so I replaced them with sunflower seeds. It tasted amazing. My family asked me to make it again for Easter and for other family gatherings. Definitely a keeper!
